title: Constitutional Law I: structure and powers
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze judicial review and justiciability, the powers of Congress (commerce, taxing and spending, and enforcement of the Civil War amendments), limits on the states (the dormant commerce clause and preemption), separation of powers and executive power, and state action.

weeks.2: Justiciability: standing, ripeness, mootness and political questions
weeks.7: Congress's power to enforce the Fourteenth Amendment

blocks.deliverable: Decide whether a federal statute fits within the commerce power.
Apply the conditions test for federal spending.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a discriminatory state law.
Apply the Youngstown framework to an executive action.
Decide whether a private actor's conduct is state action.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Bench memo: for a supplied challenge to a federal statute and a state law, written for the course, write a 2,000-word bench memo analyzing standing, federal power, preemption and the dormant commerce clause.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
